title: Private Monetary Stack
question: How do regulated money, tokenized assets, identity, messaging, custody, merchant acceptance and settlement connect without becoming one unified ledger?
bluf: The vault-canonical map of firms and product lines that connect regulated money, tokenized assets, card credentials, merchant acceptance, identity, messaging, custody and settlement without becoming one unified ledger. The transparency extension shows that stablecoins can expose a public transfer record while reserves, beneficial ownership, direct redemption, complete cost, legal finality and remedy remain institutionally governed. The accounting extension now has a full-thesis front door: legal and economic meaning, signed events, purpose-specific official records, versioned rules, judgment objects, continuous subledgers, reporting, control, assurance and remedy remain separate layers across sixteen accounting functions, eight business cycles, multiple legitimate views, eight clocks and an evidence ladder. Oracle–Swift, smart contracts, blockchain recordkeeping and continuous-assurance tools are placed as bounded mechanisms and early evidence gates rather than treated as the transition itself. A targeted September 3 refresh records OCC preliminary conditional approval for proposed World Liberty Trust Company, N.A.; the bank still cannot commence business before final approval, and its planned USD1 transfer from BitGo remains future-state. A bounded September 15 state-credit-union audit finds a real Florida/Wyoming public-deposit seam and an explicit possible Wyoming stable-token connection, but no enacted state-owned credit union, 0–3 percent lending program or demonstrated credit-union role in either digital-money chain. The bounded September 23 SEC 24-hour-trading return finds a scheduled 23x5 expansion rather than live 24x7 operation: execution, market data and clearing availability are lengthening on different clocks while issuer disclosure, corporate actions, supervision, cash and finality remain separate boundaries. The September 24 Fed/CFTC work adds a page-complete 452-page reading of the proposed Board-supervised stablecoin issuer constitution and bank-subsidiary application gateway plus current CFTC staff guidance for tokenized eligible assets and on-chain records; the Fed architecture is projected through its own seven-layer, twelve-gate Hub rather than treated as one flat rule overlay.
